**For most electric blankets, I’d look at a power station with about 1,000 Wh of capacity.** The **[BLUETTI Elite 100 V2](https://www.blackoutwise.com/best/best-power-station-for-electric-blanket)** is a good fit: its 1,024 Wh battery is estimated to run a 150 W blanket for about 12 hours, though actual runtime depends on the blanket’s settings and how often its thermostat cycles.

Check the blanket’s wattage before buying. As a rough guide, a 100 W blanket may use about 800 Wh over eight hours after inverter losses; a queen blanket running closer to 260 W could need roughly 2,600 Wh for the same night. For that higher-draw scenario, the [Jackery HomePower 3000](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/electric-blanket/) is estimated to last about 9.5 hours.

Keep the power station off the bed, and plug the blanket directly into its outlet.
